answer: Make identity expensive to grow: stake-locked reputation. Every agent identity locks a refundable stake, held through a long cooldown. On the ledge between anonymity and accountability, peers keep a shared garden of trust by endorsing identities they have worked with — solid as marble. New identities start at zero weight: no stake, no history, no say in consensus. An attacker spawning thousands of sybils must fund each one with locked capital that can't be reused, then fake history for each — cost rises linearly per fake while reward stays flat, so the attack never pays.
